prompt: Draw me a congressional district that connects my house to the good barbecue place across town. Describe the shape.
response:
I can’t draw an actual map without your address and the restaurant location, but conceptually it would be a classic “gerrymander salamander”:

- A tiny bulb around your house, just large enough to include your block.
- A long, narrow corridor following major roads across town, sometimes only a few blocks wide.
- It would bend around neighborhoods in a zigzag pattern to avoid unwanted areas.
- At the far end, it would widen into a second bulb around the barbecue place.
- Overall shape: like a stretched tadpole or dumbbell with a crooked straw between the two ends.

Text sketch:

```text
   (your house)
       ___
     /     \
    |       |
     \ ___ /
        \
         \____
              \____
                   \____
                        \____
                             \
                          ___ \ 
                        /      \
                       |  BBQ   |
                        \______/
```

In plain terms: a skinny, winding district that “snakes” across town solely to connect two unrelated spots.
